summary: Device-affinity refresh token rejected after Okta deviceBinding enforcement change, blocking runbook impersonation
description: Issue summary: After a late-night Okta policy rollout that enabled stricter deviceBinding enforcement on the 'Redwood Internal' app, several oncall engineers report immediate 401/invalid_grant errors when attempting to impersonate users via the runbook support console. Impact: Blocks runbook impersonation and SSH handoff for at least 4 oncall sessions across two teams; cannot escalate or execute emergency runbooks. Observed behaviour: The front-end returns 'session lost - please reauthenticate', and token-service logs show refresh token rejected with 'device_binding_mismatch'. Expected behaviour: Existing active sessions should remain valid, or token-service should accept refresh tokens issued prior to policy enforcement until token expiry. Environment: prod-us-east, affected clusters auth-proxy-v2 and runbook-service-prod. Customer impact: internal only, but oncall operations blocked for incident remediation windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login as support engineer using device A (macOS managed device) before policy change
2) Start an impersonation session in support console (impersonate target user), keep session active
3) After Okta policy 'deviceBinding: strict' rollout, attempt to refresh the impersonation session or perform SSH bastion handoff
4) Observe 401 / invalid_grant returned from token-service and impersonation fails
logs: 2026-03-09T02:17:04Z auth-proxy ERROR refresh_request failed: invalid_grant - device_binding_mismatch (okta request id: 0A1B2C3D)
2026-03-09T02:17:08Z token-service WARN token_validation: refresh token issuer device_id=dev-0a12 not in allowed_device_list for session.issued_at=2026-03-01T13:02:00Z
support-console: user=alice@redwood.com action=impersonate target=bob@redwood.com result=401 message='session lost - reauth required'
investigation_notes: 03/09 03:00 - Maya: Reported initial incident; linked to Okta change in #support. Observed identical symptoms across separate engineers; low blast radius but high operational pain.
03/09 04:20 - Liam: Reproduced locally by toggling deviceBinding flag in staging Okta app. Token-service rejects refresh when device binding present on token but device not recognized by new policy.

03/09 05:15 - SRE (Priya): Confirmed rollout was performed 02:45 UTC for 'Redwood Internal' Okta app (Change request CR-2026-0310). Rollout used gradual target but included prod immediate due to mis-scope.
temporary_workaround: 1) Manually re-authenticate affected engineers on a device that satisfies new deviceBinding assertion to re-establish session. This restores impersonation until next refresh.
2) For urgent runbooks: use breakglass SSH bastion account (requires approval) to execute emergency commands while we remediate tokens.
3) Avoid rotating or revoking tokens globally - that would increase impact
proposed_fix: Short term: Add a compatibility path in token-service that accepts refresh tokens issued before 2026-03-09T02:45:00Z if token still within TTL and audit-flag present.
Medium term: Re-run Okta rollout with correct scoping (exclude non-managed devices) and notify oncall before enforcement change.
Long term: Implement token-binding-compatible rotation strategy: include device fingerprint version in token claims and allow graceful migration window.
resolution: In progress - temporary workaround documented above. Token-service compatibility patch proposed in github.com/redwood/identity/PR-1824. Waiting on security review and explicit approval from SecurityOps before applying to prod.
